proposed_new_terms.definition: A background process that reviews, deduplicates, and prunes memory files during idle time, implemented via a three-gate system (time, sessions, lock) and a forked subagent.
A filesystem-based lock file whose mtime serves as the lastConsolidatedAt timestamp and whose body contains the holder's PID, preventing concurrent consolidation across processes.

A pattern for background task scheduling where progressively more expensive checks (time, workload, lock) are evaluated in order, minimizing wasted computation when upstream gates would have rejected the task.
